what: Build loop for Mole L1-L3 (D24 order). Each task runs produce -> check -> correct -> repeat until green, against checks written and committed BEFORE its code. Done = those checks pass and the evidence is saved, never the agent saying so.

method.rule: a loop is produce, check, correct, repeat until green; the check is the whole thing, written first so a program can evaluate it; absence of an error is not evidence of correctness; the graph (which tasks exist, what waits on what) is the layer above: an edge exists only if a task reads another's output

method.src: alexlavaee, Agents Write the Code. Your System Has to Prove It. (3C1 line 504; .../raw/alexlavaee_2110521585623003572_text.txt)
method.rule: done = checks the agent didn't write and can't change say the acceptance criteria are met, and their output is saved; contract before code; deterministic pyramid (types/lint, unit, integration, end-to-end) with a thin model judge on top; fresh reviewer session that never saw the implementer's transcript, findings P0-P2, review rounds capped (same blocker 3 rounds -> blocked); read the test diff before the implementation diff

loop_rules: R0 prior art first (prior-art-first skill, Raymond 10-29 'dont just make shit up pls … search up all th ebest resources alaready availble before you start building'): before the checks-first commit, tasks/<T>/4 log/prior-art.md lists the standard approaches for this exact problem (papers, open-source code, vendor docs, recent blogs, benchmarks; pages saved with URL + date), the method picked and why, and how the field measures it; the bench uses the field's metric and bar where one exists; a reviewer rejects a bench or method without it

R1 checks first: each task commits its benchmark keys + failing tests (red) in a commit of their own before any implementation commit; the keys carry a written date earlier than the first implementation commit
R2 can't change: after R1's commit the implementer never edits those keys or tests; a needed change goes to tasks/<T>/4 log/key-changes.md with the reason and waits for the reviewer (or Raymond)
R3 repeat until green: run the task's checks after every change; cap 6 rounds per task; the same failure 3 rounds in a row -> ledger blocked with the cause
R4 evidence saved: every check run appends one line to tasks/<T>/4 log/runs.jsonl {time, commit, cmd, exit, metric values}; the ledger hand-in quotes the last line

R5 fresh reviewer: a session that never saw the implementer's transcript reviews against done-when, reads the test diff first, findings P0-P2 with a reproducer; P0/P1 must be fixed or disputed with evidence
R6 deterministic first: every metric here is computed by code; a model may only word things (reasons, questions) on top of facts code already found, and is never the check
R7 never green by deleting: a check that was red may turn green only through an implementation change, never by loosening the check (R2)

end_goals.goal: when an agent changes code you knew, Mole tells you which of your understanding went stale
when a change edits lines a past fix wrote, Mole brings up that fix's reason and guarding test, beside the change, with a clickable source
at most 3 questions per change, aimed at your understanding, and none when the change touches nothing known
all of it from your own files (repo + .mole/), local, fast enough to run on every agent stop

you can see each agent run as states: what context (and which version of it) the agent had, what it already tried, what it changed, across compaction and across agents, linked to the code it touched (3C1 lines 171, 177, 232, 289-290)

the resume is the plan (Raymond 10-29): every claim in the target entry (context/product-plan/4 Resume + interview.md) is made true by a task here and measured by a metric; the page counts how many are true today
verify at the hand-back (3C1 'verificatn: sure thing u tell it to do actually done'): the tests that matter run, an agent's claims are checked against its transcript, one verdict
the decisions behind the code (D31, his 3C1 268/301/652/676): records with citator flags, rules that cite the why, on the file tree, in one team check
what actually runs: runtime call edges from tests where the static graph is blind

end_goals.what: the whole product works where people already are: VS Code view + hover + file tree + Problems, the agent plugin and MCP, the team server, each serving the decisions behind the code

metrics.target: recall 100%, false flags <= 5%, whitespace/comment-only edits never flagged

metrics.name: since-you-last-looked precision / recall

metrics.target: precision 100%, recall 100% on the fixture; unseen symbols never listed

metrics.name: question usefulness

metrics.name: hand-back test selection
metrics.how: 10 planted regressions in Mole + Excalidraw, key written before the code; select by past-fix lineage (T12) + call-graph reachability, run with vitest

metrics.name: hand-back verify gate
